featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tanjore Tiffin Room, Versova – Authentic South Indian Delight!

Visited **Tanjore Tiffin Room, Versova** on Sunday with a group of 12, and the experience was fantastic!

The **Chicken Ghee Roast, Chicken Chintamani, and Pepper Chicken** were absolutely outstanding - rich, spicy, and packed with authentic South Indian flavors. 🍗🔥
We also loved the **Malabar Parotta, Appam, Idiyappam, and Dosa with Sambar** - soft, fresh, and perfect with the curries.

Veg dishes like **Jackfruit Cutlet and Jackfruit Biryani** were surprisingly delicious, and the **Chicken Biryani** was aromatic and generously portioned. The **Mango Mint Cooler** was a refreshing highlight after the spicy feast. 🥭❄️

If the main seating area is full, they have **additional seating inside WTF**, which is very convenient during peak hours.
They also offer a **tasting platter where the staff explains different curries and how they are used in cooking** - a brilliant concept for first-time visitors and food enthusiasts.

The restaurant is **just ~500 meters from Versova Metro Station**, making it very easy to reach. 🚇

For around **₹9.7K for 12 people (~₹800 per person)**, the quality, quantity, and taste were totally worth it.

**Highly recommended for authentic South Indian food and group outings! Will definitely visit again.**

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is quite popular and is usually packed during both lunch and dinner, so making a reservation is a must. This was my second visit here, and of course we ordered their signature Railway Curry it never disappoints.

This time we also tried:
Mutton Cutlet
Mini Idlis
Veg Cutlet
Beef Roast with Lemon Rice
Egg Appams
Fried prawns

The mini idlis with ghee were absolutely delicious, and the beef roast was our next favourite.
Fried prawns was crispy and had a balanced taste.

I had high expectations from the mutton cutlet, but it didn’t quite live up to the hype. The lemon rice and egg appam were also slightly on the sweeter side, which didn’t go too well with our palate.

Their chutneys are amazing though definitely a highlight!

The staff is extremely warm and courteous, and the ambience is lovely. They even have a pet dog at the restaurant, but do be careful as it may suddenly run up or try to bite if you get too close.

Overall, a charming place with great service and some standout dishes, but a few items could be improved taste-wise.

Filter Coffee – Strong, creamy, and the perfect ending to a wholesome South Indian meal.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Banana Leaf is a great place for anyone who loves authentic vegetarian South Indian food. We tried a few of their delicacies—filter coffee, appam, and the Benne Podi Masala Dosa.
My absolute favorite was the Benne Podi Masala Dosa. It’s not like the traditional benne dosa that comes drenched in coconut oil—this version is neat, easy to eat, and definitely feels healthier. It’s served with white butter (makkhan), flavorful chutney, and sambar, which perfectly balance the dosa.
The filter coffee was comforting and well brewed, and the appam was soft and light. They have a wide range of South Indian delicacies on the menu, and there’s a lot more I’m looking forward to trying.
I’ll definitely keep updating my reviews as and when we visit again. For now, the Benne Podi Masala Dosa is completely on my mind and a must-try! 😋

We started with the Coorg Idli, which was extremely soft, fluffy, and comforting. The Benne Podi Masala Dosa was a clear highlight — perfectly crispy, generously topped with podi and butter, and served with flavorful sambhar and fresh white chutney.
We also tried the Malgudi Special Tiffin, which is a complete and satisfying meal. It includes rice with options like lemon rice or tomato rice, one Malabar paratha, and a choice of curry between Malabar or Chettinad, both rich in flavour and well-balanced. The pineapple sheera was a nice sweet ending, light and refreshing. Beverage options like filter coffee, buttermilk, and masala chai make the experience even better.
The food truly reflects simple, authentic South Indian flavours. With around 13 outlets across Mumbai, Malgudi Simply South is a great option for anyone craving quality South Indian comfort food.

I visited KTR (Karnataka Tiffin Room) for a quick breakfast and honestly, I was fanboying the entire time. If you’re looking for authentic Karnataka flavors, this is it.

​The Food: The Open Masala Podi Davangere Dosa was bang on, crispy, buttery, and perfectly spiced. The Idli with Neer Chutney was incredibly comforting, and the Cold Filter Coffee was the perfect refreshing end to the meal.
​
Don't be fooled by the exterior! Inside, it’s a whole different vibe with lovely, soft Kannada songs playing in the background. It’s mostly self-service, the food comes out super quick, and it is incredibly value for money. Highly recommended for a soul-satisfying South Indian fix!

featured_reviews.name: Ninad joshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
After having early morning Pune-to-Mumbai travel, we were searching for a good and refreshing South Indian breakfast point, and we found this place while en route to home.

It’s not a fancy fine dining place, but it is a traditional place where the smell of filter coffee hits you the moment you walk in. It’s simple, clean, and perfect for a quick delicious meal.

We had 1 Podi Thatte Idali, 1 Benne plain dosa and 1 Benne Podi plain dosa.

Benne Plain Dosa – Simply tasty, it's crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and golden-browned with an ample amount of desi ghee.

​

Benne Podi Dosa - The podi powder is nutty and spicy Bangalore-style milagai podi. The inner part of the dosa is generously sprinkled with the podi masala and loaded with desi ghee. It’s spicy enough to give you a kick but balanced with ghee.

It was a nice experience for us, and I will definitely recommend this place if you are looking for South Indian food.

featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Patodia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst restaurant experience of my life.

Everything from ordering to eating was a complete mess. The restaurant itself looked like it was either being demolished or under renovation. Temporary green sheets were hanging around, the setup looked unfinished and unorganized, and there was no proper seating arrangement — we had to stand.

We initially ordered Meetha Bhath, Devanagari Masala Dosa, Idli and Medu Vada through the kiosk and paid ₹588. After payment, the receipt did not print. The manager then took our order on WhatsApp and informed us that only Idli and Benne Dosa were available. Instead of refunding unavailable items, we were asked to replace our order with whatever was left.

The ghee podi idli arrived first. The idli itself was okay, but the chutney tasted sour and seemed spoiled, especially in this heat. We asked for tissue paper — out of stock. Asked for drinking water from their own menu — out of stock. Ordered filter coffee — tasted more like melted Coffee Bite chocolate than actual filter coffee.

After waiting almost 20 minutes for dosa, staff first attempted to serve us someone else’s order. When our dosa finally arrived, both dosas had no salt at all. We refused to eat them and asked for a refund. After arguing with the manager for nearly 15 minutes, we finally got the refund, only to then discover that they were apparently out of salt too.

What made it worse was that the staff seemed completely unapologetic through the entire experience. There was no ownership, concern, or effort to make things right.

A restaurant can run out of an item or two, but running out of menu items, tissues, water, salt and basic organization is unbelievable. The place also looked poorly maintained and gave an unhygienic impression overall. Looking at the setup in the photos, it did not feel like a place ready to serve customers. Extremely disappointing.

The restaurant seemed to be under renovation or in a temporary setup, with no proper seating arrangements and an unfinished environment. From a customer perspective, it did not feel clean or properly maintained.

We placed an order through the kiosk for multiple items and paid ₹588, but the receipt failed to print. Later we were informed that most items were unavailable and were asked to modify the order instead of receiving a refund.

The idli was acceptable, but the chutney tasted sour. Tissues and drinking water were unavailable, which was surprising. The filter coffee also did not meet expectations.

After a long wait, our dosa arrived after staff initially attempted to hand us an incorrect order. The dosas themselves had no salt and were inedible. We eventually requested a refund and had to spend additional time discussing it with the manager.

The experience was further affected by the staff’s attitude, which felt unapologetic despite multiple issues during the visit.

Basic inventory management, customer communication and cleanliness standards need significant improvement.

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're craving authentic Karnataka-style breakfast in Mumbai, Karnataka Tiffin Room in Versova, Andheri West is an absolute must-visit! I recently stopped by and went all out with their menu – and I'm so glad I did.
What I ordered:
Started with the Davanagere Benne Masala Dosa – and wow, this was the star of the show! Crispy, buttery, and generously loaded with the perfect spiced potato filling. The benne (butter) was clearly not compromised on, giving it that rich, indulgent taste that Davanagere is famous for.
The Bengaluru Ghee Podi Plain Dosa was another winner. Simple yet packed with flavor from the gunpowder spice mix and pure ghee. If you love that smoky, spicy kick, this one's for you.
The Ghee Podi Thatte Idli was soft, fluffy, and beautifully soaked in ghee with the podi adding just the right amount of heat. Comfort food at its finest!
For something sweet, the Kesari Bath hit the spot – perfectly textured, not too sweet, with the aroma of ghee and cardamom. A beautiful way to round off the meal.
And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without filter coffee. I tried both the cold and hot filter coffee – both were strong, aromatic, and had that authentic decoction taste. The cold coffee was refreshing, while the hot one was the perfect companion to the crispy dosas.
Overall experience: The food is legit, the portions are generous, and the authenticity shines through every dish. Service was quick, and the vibe is casual and welcoming. Prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity you get.
Highly recommend for anyone who takes their South Indian breakfast seriously! Will definitely be back for more.
Must-try: Davanagere Benne Masala Dosa and Filter Coffee (both versions!)

featured_reviews.name: Suhel Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
With all the benne dosa buzz around the city, decided to give this place a try! It’s a small outlet with simple wooden benches along the walls and a couple of tables in the center for those who prefer to stand and eat.

Reached early around 7 AM (as per their opening time), but only idli, wada, and coffee were available. The popular Davangere dosa, prepared on a woodfire, was available only after 8 AM — a bit disappointing since that’s the main highlight of the place.

The Medu Wada and Dal Wada were fresh, crisp, and served with chutney (no sambar). The Davangere Benne Open Dosa had a thicker, softer texture compared to the usual — topped with mild potato filling, chutney, and a generous layer of benne (butter). The Bangalore Dosa was authentic and slightly smaller in size, but the rich ghee made it satisfying — perfectly golden, crisp on the outside and soft inside, paired with flavorful chutneys (again, no sambar).

The filter coffee was spot-on — strong, aromatic, and served the traditional way.

Overall, a great alternative if you want to enjoy authentic benne dosa without standing in long queues, and at more reasonable pricing too.

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: A masterclass in texture and spice, the Chole Samosa Chaat here is a sensory riot where the shattered, golden crunch of the samosa is beautifully surrendered to a deep, tangy chickpea curry, all elevated by a cooling drizzle of yogurt and the electric snap of fresh chutneys. To recreate this at home, simmer boiled chickpeas in a masala of onions, ginger-garlic, and amchoor, then ladle it over crushed hot samosas and finish with a snowfall of fine sev and chopped onions. In a sophisticated contrast, the Rava Dosa arrives as a shatteringly crisp, lacy veil of gold; its secret lies in a buttermilk-thin batter of semolina, rice flour, and cumin poured from a height onto a screaming-hot griddle until it develops its signature "Swiss-cheese" holes. Whether you’re diving into the indulgent, street-style chaos of the chaat or the ethereal, buttery crispness of the dosa, this is a dual-course experience that perfectly celebrates the diverse landscape of Indian soul food.

First of all Salutations to Shri Pravin Shetty and many thanks to Shri Sudesh Rai as well. Our Wadhwani family have been regular visitors here, ever since our children joined H.M.P.School in 2000-2001. We visited here for lunch today after a long gap of nearly 7/8 years. Pleasantly inviting as always, the management is constantly involved in seating the customers, guiding the stewards and waiters to unattended tables, especially during rush hours, thereby raising the standards of hospitality to a new high.
They have both AC (higher prices) and non-AC sections. Waiting time for AC usually is 15 minutes or more, unless you reach early by 12.15 or 12.30 pm for lunch. We chose the non-AC with good overhead fans, since we were hungry and it was nearly 2 pm.
A heartfelt thanks to Sanjay and his colleagues for the impeccable service provided today and attention to detail.
We had a mix of Cheese Pav Bhaji, Puri Bhaji, Benne Masala Dosa, Rava Masala Dosa and Mysore Masala Dosa with a side order of Sweet Lassi for all.
Each item was served hot, with the regular accompaniments, onion, lime, specially requested pickle, hot sambhar and coconut chutney.
They serve cold Distilled water in Stainless steel glasses, which bypasses the need for any bottled mineral water.
Good quality tissues and an easily accessible washbasin make it convenient for clean up after a finger licking, palate tickling vegetarian meal. Being 100% vegetarian is the added advantage here. They accept all kinds of payments with no extra surcharge or service charges. The regulatory 5% GST is added to your bill amount.
A good hearty meal for five cost us less than 1500 including tips.
Even if you are very hungry and are good eaters, surely you won't spend more than 400-450 per person at this absolutely genuine vegetarian restaurant catering mostly to the College and school kids, especially during day time and the locals living in Andheri West, especially in the evenings.
Valet parking is available.
Latest menu shared here. A separate Fire of Mexico menu, includes Starters, Main course, salads, pasta n rice available . Speciality juices and milkshakes too.

They also provide Home Delivery albeit at slightly higher prices than in-house eating.  Home delivery menu also attached here.

Do visit with peace of mind. Be calm and relaxed. Being hypertensive creates a foul atmosphere for yourselves. Enjoy and return smiling.

It's a really beautiful place (architecture wise only), near Kokilaben Hospital, and you can go here just to see the architecture, skip the food.
We were 8 of us, luckily we went early and got a table, The cafe does not allow reservations, so you might have to wait in a long queue even to get in. Even if you say you have friends sitting inside, then they have to come to the door to bring you inside. The table was not really comfortable for 8 people. And some people have to stand and eat.
❌Food: 2/5
We ordered Benne dosa, it was served cold, thrice.
Benne podi dosa  was served hot, and it was ok.
I ordered butter milk and it was good.
People liked cold coffee.
A friend who ordered hot coffee did not like it.
Tamarind rice was served cold, had no taste at all, and in fact had a bit of bitter taste.
Curd rice was decent.
Bisi bele bhaat was ok ok.
❌Service: 2/5 Service was pretty average, as you have to stand in a queue in front of the automated touch screen ordering. (One of the kiosks was not working when we went there). Also the place is huge, so they call out your order number, but then most of the times you will not really hear it (could be one of the reasons why our food was always cold). The place feels overly crowded like a railway station.
✅Ambiance: 4/5 Architect has done a great job, and deserves an award to create a beautiful place at such a noisy road. This is the only thing you should go for. Though the wash basin is outside the facility. So in case you like washing hands before eating, then wash them before getting in the queue.
❌Value: We ended up spending about 300 per head, which was a decent amount, but not at all worth going again. If you have to stand and wait here, then go to any other south indian restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

featured_reviews.name: Mudit Bansal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshinayan in Juhu is a highly recommended, budget-friendly spot for anyone seeking authentic South Indian cuisine in Mumbai. Despite its simple decor, it remains a favorite among locals and celebrities for its consistently delicious food and quick hospitality.

Ambiance and Service
The restaurant features a peaceful, straightforward dining environment where staff serve guests in traditional South Indian attire. Because of its immense popularity, visitors should anticipate a wait time of 30 to 45 minutes, especially during weekends. Fortunately, once you are seated, the kitchen operates with remarkable efficiency and brings out orders within minutes.

Food and Specialties
The menu focuses heavily on perfectly executed classic staples that are incredibly flavourful and reasonably priced. Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. Large groups can enjoy a massive 4-foot long family dosa, and every visit should conclude with a hot cup of their signature filter coffee.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We were a party of 3 for lunch on a Wednesday . Getting a table was easy as we were there around 12.00 noon. Around 12.30pm the restaurant was practically full.
The seating is spread out , the space is nice and bright and very clean . The aircon facing us was on high cool so we had them turn it down and they obliged .
The food was amazing - for drinks we had the fresh sugar cane juice ,filter coffee and fresh lime soda , all of which were really good - the coffee could have been hotter .
Starters we had rasam vada & kancheepuram idli to share - both were well made - vada was soft and so was the idli. The rasam was top notch.
Mains we shared a ghee masala dosa , masala vada and pesarattu -all three were really good .
Desserts we had were falooda kulfi, kesar pista kulfi and filter coffee affogato. All three did not disappoint.
Service would have been 5* except for a very reluctant server who stood across the table staring at everything but did not take orders or help.
The restaurant sells two kinds of podi and rasam/ sambar powder in their own brand .
